frequency_question: How often does the central bank invoke targeted incremental reserve requirements during periods of sudden banking system liquidity surges?
membership_rule: Includes any formal regulatory notification or monetary policy statement introducing an incremental, temporary cash reserve ratio (or structurally identical marginal reserve requirement) applied to deposit growth above a baseline date. Excludes standard, permanent changes to the headline cash reserve ratio.

cases.name: Demonetisation-driven temporary incremental CRR of November 2016

provenance_note: rate of 100% from only 2 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 2 named episodes in 25 years where temporary incremental reserve requirements were deployed to mop up acute liquidity gluts.
known_gaps: Excludes general repo-rate adjustments and standard variable rate reverse repo (VRRR) auctions, which are frequent routine operations rather than special incremental reserve mandates.
skeleton: Instances of severe, unanticipated surges in banking system liquidity (e.g., systemic shocks, sudden deposit inflows, or structural FX interventions) prompting emergency liquidity management tools over multi-decade policy cycles.
multiplier: 2 hits across 2 distinct systemic liquidity surge epochs in 25 years.
validity_reason: Central banking statutory frameworks and liquidity management toolkits evolve slowly over multi-year regulatory regimes.
